sources.title: Uniform sampling and time-axis calculations
sources.details: Uniform sampling: t_n=n/fs and duration convention T=N/fs (N uniformly spaced sample intervals of audio, not last-minus-first time coordinate). For 1600 samples:1600/16000=0.1,1600/8000=0.2. A 440Hz sinusoid has period1/440, so samples/period=fs/440=36.363636... or18.181818... (not necessarily an integer because the cycle boundary need not hit a sample). Nyquist=fs/2 gives8000 and4000. For integer n, sin(2*pi*(fs-f)*n/fs)=sin(2*pi*n-2*pi*f*n/fs)=-sin(2*pi*f*n/fs)=sin(2*pi*f*n/fs+pi). Thus9000=16000-7000 and9500=16000-6500 fold with opposite sine phase for all n, not only the displayed prefix. If the same array is played at fs_new, sin(2*pi*f*n/fs_old)=sin(2*pi*(f*fs_new/fs_old)*(n/fs_new)); 440*8000/16000=220 and duration doubles. A function or fixed output distribution of identical sample arrays cannot uniquely identify two distinct underlying signals without extra assumptions/side information. Proper resampling instead keeps physical time t and computes new samples; N_new=N_old*fs_new/fs_old when integral. Here4591*2=9182; both4591/8000=9182/16000=0.573875. Exercise8000/8000=1 second requires16000 samples at16000Hz. These exact identities are separated from float32 numerical errors checked in a1.
